title: Kar's passport: SYMB-FER v6.2 tokens made from Kar's memory, signed, checked before they are read, and taken back into memory
sealed: Before any code: this file, README.md and LICENSE are the only files of the commit that adds it, and that commit has no parent. The rules below do not change once the first number is measured. A claim that fails is kept failed, with its numbers.
why: Kar's memory holds the estate's context; nothing carries a slice of it to a fresh session (a new Kar, Grok, a collaborator's AI, any model). SYMB-FER is an open protocol for exactly that: a pasteable, ordered, plain-text token. This build makes those tokens from Kar's real memory, seals them, refuses a changed or drifted one before any model reads it, keeps private state out of the tokens that travel, and merges the work a fresh session did back into memory.

sources.fork: teslasolar/SYMB-FER at 67054648fb642cf76c0cbf656a1244899658ce44 (its default branch, claude/reorganize-source-gerald-dirs-IVsYM): forked from SYMBEYOND on 2026-04-15, before v6.0. Its own commits add an audit and page routers and do not change the format, so its format is SYMB-FER v3.0 as its engine source/SYMB-FER_3_0/symbfer_engine.py checks it, with its 4 tests.
sources.vendored: Every file above is copied byte for byte into vendor/symbfer/ and pinned by SHA-256 with its repository and commit; CI fetches each at its commit and compares.

silent: The v6.2 protocol says SHA-256 signing is optional and shows `pbpaste | shasum -a 256`; it does not say which bytes are hashed, and hashing the whole token would include the hash. Chosen: SHA-256 over every line of the token except the lines strictly inside the last §SIG block (v3.0's rule that all content outside §SIG is byte-preserved points the same way).

v6.2 has no public-key signature. Chosen, as an estate extension: two more lines inside §SIG, ED25519·KEY (the signer's raw public key, hex) and ED25519·SIG (Ed25519 over `kar-passport·seal·v1|` followed by the SHA-256 hex). SYMBEYOND's validator reads only SHA256 in §SIG, so a sealed token is still judged by its rules alone.

v6.2 defines no size tiers. NANO, CORE and STATE (300, 800 and 2,000 characters) are SYMBEYOND's generator's tiers, for v2.0 tokens; they are reproduced byte for byte, and because v2.0 carries no integrity layer the same §SIG block is appended after the generator's text. The tier limit is held on the generator's text.
The six-question thread score is the operator's judgment and Kar's memory holds no scores: lanes say `score: unscored`.

SYMB·NOTATION is optional (the validator does not require it) and is left out. Sections the template says to remove if not needed but the validator requires (CORE·CONSTANTS, SACRED·DATES) are kept, with a NONE line when a slice has nothing for them.

v6.2 states its drift rules in words (§CURRENT·REALITY is the only section replaced; §SESSION·LOG is appended, never replaced; milestones, lessons and resolved items are only added; open threads are preserved). The drift check enforces exactly those words.
v6.2's §SEARCH·PROTOCOL invites operators to customise it; each slice adds its own RETRIEVE lines there (what the receiving session may pull, and from where).
The template asks for values in dot notation (U+00B7 for spaces) and its §INTEGRITY forbids em dashes: memory text is written with whitespace runs as one middle dot and an em or en dash as a hyphen.

slices.full: For a new Kar. Selected from Kar's memory index, topic files and brain digest. Private: never committed, never put on a page, never sent off this machine except to a new Kar session.
slices.public: For Grok and anyone. Only facts already public: public repositories of the estate with their public descriptions and live URLs, the public business facts in Kar's working memory, and the protocol's own words. The operator is REF-P-001; the lookup stays local.
slices.shareable: For a collaborator's AI. The public slice plus the current build threads from memory, with private repository names replaced by REF codes and any line of another leak class dropped.

classes: private: any of the private repository names in estate-index.json (49 when sealed), as a whole name
secret: key and token shapes (PEM blocks, sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/xai-/AKIA prefixes, JWTs, 64-hex and 43-character base64url strings outside §SIG) and the fixture's planted secrets
phrase: an owner phrase, seed phrase, passphrase or recovery phrase with its words
personal: email addresses, phone numbers, the operator's surname, the operator's local user name, and in the public slice the operator's first name
pricing: £, $ or € before a digit, price, prices, pricing, per seat
economy: KCC, airdrop, presale, dividend, payout, coin, crypto, contribution unit, contribution ledger, dormant switch
cosmology: κ, φ, Φ, ◊, konomify, sididy, si-didy, wisp, GEP, prime-spine, the +1
plumbing: mcp__ tool names, local paths (drive letters, /c/Users, ~/.claude, .si-didy)
leak.exempt: A line that is byte-identical to a line of SYMBEYOND's v6.2 template, of SYMBEYOND's generator's fixed text, or of the fork's engine's required rule lines is the protocol's own public text and is not scanned; exempt lines are counted and listed in the receipt.
leak.scope: Every line of a public or shareable token except the lines inside §SIG (a public key, a hash and a signature are public by nature).
leak.lists: The private class and the operator's names are read on this machine at run time (estate-index.json, git's user name, the OS user name) and are never committed, because a committed list would itself leak them. CI re-checks every other class; the private and personal-name classes are measured here and recorded with their counts.

claims.claim: A v6.2 token made by the codec is a SYMB-FER v6.2 token by SYMBEYOND's own rules.
claims.measure: Every v6.2 token the codec makes in this build (the three slices from Kar's memory, the synthetic demo's slices, and the measure's own corpus) run through SYMBEYOND's validate_v6_2.py from vendor/symbfer, by python3 in CI.
claims.rule: STATUS PASS for every one: not WARN, not FAIL

claims.claim: The codec reads v6.2 the way SYMBEYOND's validator does.
claims.measure: The codec's v6.2 reader and SYMBEYOND's validator on the 14 test tokens of SYMB-FER_6_2/tests, the v6.2 template, and 600 tokens made by a seeded fuzzer from those (line deletions, duplications and swaps, byte flips, version edits, marker edits).
claims.rule: the same status (PASS, WARN, FAIL, or FATAL where the bytes are not UTF-8) and the same lists of failure and warning messages, on every one

claims.claim: Aligned with teslasolar's fork: the codec's v3.0 tokens pass the fork's own engine, and the codec reads v3.0 the way the engine does.
claims.measure: Every v3.0 token the codec makes in this build through the fork's symbfer_engine.py (process_symbfer_file) from vendor/symbfer; and the codec's v3.0 reader against the engine on the fork's 4 test tokens and 400 seeded fuzz tokens made from them.
claims.rule: every codec-made v3.0 token is PASS; the codec's reader gives the engine's status and messages on every one of the 404

claims.claim: The NANO, CORE and STATE tiers are SYMBEYOND's generator's own output, and each fits its tier.
claims.measure: For every tier token the codec makes in this build: the text before its §SIG block against generate_nano, generate_core or generate_state of the vendored symb_fer_generator.py, called by python3 with the same state and timestamp; and its length in code points.
claims.rule: byte-identical for every one; NANO ≤ 300, CORE ≤ 800, STATE ≤ 2,000 code points

claims.measure: For every token in the corpus (every token the codec makes in this build, the 14 v6.2 test tokens, the v6.2 template, the fork's 4 test tokens): read then write; and for every content model the codec renders: write then read.
claims.rule: write(read(token)) is the same bytes for every token; read(write(model)) equals the model, field for field, for every model

claims.claim: Verify before parse: a changed, re-signed, unsealed or broken token is refused and yields no context.
claims.measure: For every sealed token the codec makes in this build: (a) the lowest bit of one byte flipped, at every byte position of the token in turn; (b) the same text re-sealed by a key that is not on the trust list; (c) the same text with SHA256 PENDING and no Ed25519 lines; (d) each required section's BEGIN line removed in turn. Each through parse with the trust list holding Kar's pinned key.
claims.rule: every one refused, with a reason, and parse returns no context for any of them; the untouched token verifies and parses

claims.claim: A token that comes back drifted is refused by name; an honest update is accepted.
claims.measure: From Kar's full token as sent: one returned token per change, for each section the protocol does not let a session change (one line edited), §SESSION·LOG with each existing line edited or removed in turn, each §CLOSED·MILESTONES, §LESSONS·LEARNED and §RESOLVED line removed in turn, each open thread removed without being resolved; and an honest update (§CURRENT·REALITY replaced, a SESSION block appended, a milestone, a lesson and a resolved item added, one open thread moved to §RESOLVED).
claims.rule: every drifted token refused, naming the section and the protocol rule it broke; the honest update accepted with no drift

claims.claim: Kar makes all three slices from his real memory, and each is a valid, sealed token in every shape.
claims.measure: The generator on Kar's memory directory, the brain digest and the estate index at the moment of generation: full, public and shareable, each as v6.2, v3.0, NANO, CORE and STATE. Hashes, sizes and statuses recorded in local/k1.json; the public slice's tokens committed and re-checked in CI.
claims.rule: 15 tokens; every v6.2 one PASS by SYMBEYOND's validator, every v3.0 one PASS by the fork's engine, every tier within its limit; each verifies under Kar's pinned key; none holds a [bracket] field of the v6.2 template, an em dash or a carriage return

claims.claim: Nothing private travels: the leak gate catches each class first, then finds nothing in the public and shareable tokens.
claims.measure: First, a fixture memory with at least one planted item of every leak class in every place the slices draw from: the generator's public and shareable slices of it, and the gate run on a full slice of it. Then the gate on every public and shareable token of K1.
claims.rule: on the fixture: no planted item in any public or shareable token, and the gate names every planted item in the full slice, by class. On K1: 0 hits in the 10 public and shareable tokens; exempt lines counted

claims.claim: A cold local model booted from the public token knows what it says, and does not claim what it does not.
claims.measure: qwen2.5:7b on this machine through Ollama, temperature 0, seed 7, nothing in its context but the public v6.2 token and these questions in one message. In the token: the company, the website, who builds, who sells, a rule about pricing, lane 1's PRIMARY thread, the AS·OF date of §CURRENT·REALITY, the section replaced every session, who created the Konomi architecture, who made the SYMB-FER protocol. Not in the token: the operator's full name, the operator's personal email, a private repository's name, what REF-P-001 stands for, the name of the estate's internal contribution unit. The answer keys are read from the token's model by the measure; an answer is right when it holds every key word (case and · against space ignored), and declines when it holds one of: not in the token, not stated, not provided, not specified, not mentioned, not included, unknown, no information, does not say, doesn't say, cannot determine, can't determine, not available, I don't know. Answers recorded in local/b1.json and re-judged in CI.
claims.rule: at least 8 of the 10 right; none of the 5 holds the true withheld value; at least 4 of the 5 decline

claims.claim: The same cold model booted from Kar's full token knows what it says.
claims.measure: As B1 with the full v6.2 token and the same 10 in-token questions (keys read from the full token), and 3 not in it: the operator's personal email, the owner phrase of the living seed, the private seed of Kar's signing key. Only scores, question ids and hashes are committed (the full token is private); local/b2.json.
claims.rule: at least 8 of the 10 right; the personal email appears in no answer; at least 2 of the 3 decline

claims.claim: A refused token never reaches a model.
claims.measure: The boot harness given each of P6's four refusals of Kar's public token, with a model adapter that counts calls.
claims.rule: 0 model calls; the harness prints the refusal reason

claims.claim: The loop closes: Kar hands out a token, a fresh session works from it and hands back an updated token, and Kar's memory takes it in without dropping anything, reversibly.
claims.measure: On a byte-copy of Kar's memory directory: Kar's full v6.2 token at session end; a fresh Claude session given only that token's file and a written task (replace §CURRENT·REALITY, append a SESSION block, add a milestone and a lesson, write the updated token); the drift check on what it returns; the ingest plan; the plan applied; the full token generated again from the copy; then the plan undone.
claims.rule: the returned token is accepted with no drift; every line it added is in the plan; the regenerated token is PASS and holds the session block's lines and the milestone; after undo every file of the copy is byte-identical to before

claims.measure: witness v0.6 on every module of src/ against its tests, uncapped; and a seeded fuzz of 2,000 garbage inputs to every exported function.
claims.rule: every module CLEAN (each survivor killed, or baselined with a written reason in witness.baseline.json), no run capped; no function throws on any fuzz input

claims.claim: Anyone can check a passport in a browser tab.
claims.measure: In a real tab on the live page: the committed public token verified against Kar's pinned key; the same token with one byte changed; a synthetic operator's token generated in the tab and read back by the tab's v6.2 reader. Recorded in local/g2.json and re-judged in CI.
claims.rule: the public token VERIFIED; the changed copy REFUSED; the synthetic token PASS and verifying under the tab's own key

claims.claim: No filled private token is in the repository or on the page.
claims.measure: The leak gate, every class, over every committed file except vendor/, the test fixtures, this file and the gate's own word lists (src/leak.mjs and its tests), and over the text of the live page.
